title: StudyGotchi biome layout (version 2)
description: One biome = one landmass = one course. This file is the single contract between the biome designers (docs/design/world/layouts/*.layout.json) and the generic renderer in prototypes/biome-lab/. Units: metres everywhere. Axes: x east, z south (toward the default camera), y up; settled ground is y = 0 and never changes with progress. Angles: laneYaw in radians from +z toward +x; azimuths in degrees from +z toward +x. Colours are lowercase 6-digit hex. Bands are the five progress steps 0 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 % keyed as the strings "0", "25", "50", "75", "100". Field names mirror prototypes/biome-lab/src/layout/biome-layout.ts wherever the concept matches (shape.kind, vertices, centreline, width, band, anchor, population, laneYaw, stationAzimuth, seaLevel, groundHeight, worldExtent -> world.extent, frameRadius, miniIsland -> soloIsland, headland -> landmark.plinth, range -> land.skyline.range). Anything the generic renderer does not interpret lives in a documented `extras` object so no design intent is lost.

version.description: Schema version. Always 2 for this schema; version 1 files were the designers' free-form drafts.

biome.description: Kebab-case biome id, identical to the file stem (`<biome>.layout.json`) and to the sheet `docs/design/world/biomes/<biome>.md`.

name.description: Display name of the biome family, as it appears in the course picker.

status.description: Optional free-text status line (draft date, what it is waiting on). Not read by the renderer.

notes.description: Designer notes that do not fit a field: conventions, provenance, normalisation history. Each entry is one sentence or paragraph. Not read by the renderer.

palette.description: Palette roles -> hex. Roles are free-form names used by `material` fields and by the sheet's palette table (e.g. lawn, paving, brick, water, window, accent, sky, skyNight, fog). Every value must be a colour; non-colour palette parameters belong in `ambient`.

scale.description: Size rules that keep creatures readable (fix plan Review 2: creature ~1.8 m and >= 6 % of the viewport at the district station; houses 4.5-6 m; >= 20 m of empty ground between districts).

creatureHeight.description: Resident base height in metres before `creatureScale`.

creatureScale.description: Per-biome creature scale multiplier chosen so the resident reaches >= 6 % of viewport height at every district station (biome-layout.ts `creatureScale`).

houseHeight.description: [min, max] house height in metres for the ordinary residential building kind.

hallHeight.description: [min, max] height in metres for the biome's large hall / civic / industrial building kind, if it has one.

minCreatureViewportFraction.description: The scale rule: minimum fraction of the viewport height a creature covers at a district station (0.06).

minDistrictGap.description: Minimum clear ground between any two district outlines, metres (20).

pixelCellPx.description: Fixed pixel-pass cell size in screen pixels at every station (Review 2: 2).

additionalProperties.description: Further named heights or scales specific to the family (e.g. dormHeight, bellTowerHeight): a number or a [min, max] pair in metres.

world.description: Terrain frame and vertical datum. The renderer builds a heightfield of half-extent `extent`; the land continues past it into fog at the back.

extent.description: Terrain mesh half-extent in metres (biome-layout.ts `worldExtent`). Coordinates in this file lie within [-extent, extent] on x and z; 100 = the 200 x 200 m authoring frame.

frameRadius.description: Radius in metres that the overview / arrival camera stations frame (biome-layout.ts `frameRadius`).

seaLevel.description: Water surface height in metres (y). Negative means below the settled ground.

groundHeight.description: Settled ground surface height in metres (y). The coast cliff drop is groundHeight - seaLevel. Ground never changes with progress.

relief.description: Rolling relief amplitude on the mainland in metres (soft heightfield noise; no plateaus, no discs).

land.description: The one landmass: its outline, the skyline element at its back that is the only thing allowed to grow in height, and how its coast is cut.

outline.description: Land footprint at settled-ground height. Either an explicit polygon (edges marked `openEdges` are frame edges or the skyline foot, not coasts) or an `open-back` lobe union in the style of biome-layout.ts `mainland` for procedurally wobbled coasts. Everything outside the outline (and outside `soloIsland`) is water.

vertices.description: Polygon vertices [x, z] in metres, any winding, no repeated closing point.

openEdges.description: Which frame sides of the polygon are NOT coastlines: `back` (z = -extent, the skyline foot dissolving into fog), `west`, `east` (land continues off-frame), `front` (rare). The renderer draws no cliff there.

description.description: One-line description of the land shape for the panel and the README.

kind.description: Open-back lobe union: an ellipse plus extra lobes; the back edge is cut open into the skyline.

center.description: Centre [x, z] of the main ellipse.

rx.description: Main ellipse half-width along x, metres.

rz.description: Main ellipse half-depth along z, metres.

lobes.description: Extra circular lobes [x, z, radius] unioned onto the ellipse for bays and points (biome-layout.ts `mainland.lobes`).

description.description: One-line description of the land shape.

skyline.description: The back-of-world silhouette (mountain range, gantry wall, spire rows, hall skyline...). It is the ONLY elevation that grows, driven by the course fraction; settled ground never rises.

kind.description: Skyline family. Known kinds: mountain-range (ice, alpine), gantry-wall (heavy industry), spire-rows (future utopia), hall-skyline (academy town), cream-peaks (candy world). Any other kebab-case string is allowed for new families; the renderer falls back to generic blocks of `growth[band].height`.

description.description: What the skyline is made of and how it reads at 48 px.

arc.description: The skyline's spine as a polyline [x, z] from west to east (>= 2 points). For the parametric families this is z = arcZ + arcCurve * x^2 sampled every 20 m; `range` keeps the parameters.

range.description: Parametric form of the arc mirroring biome-layout.ts `range`: z = arcZ + arcCurve * x^2; the land's back boundary sits `footDepth` in front of the arc and the foothill belt climbs `footRise` metres toward it.

arcZ.description: z of the arc at x = 0, metres (negative = toward the back).

arcCurve.description: Curvature coefficient; the arc ends wrap forward for positive values.

footDepth.description: Distance in metres from the arc forward to the skyline foot (where districts may start).

footRise.description: Height gain in metres from the foot to the arc (0 for flat-plinth skylines).

footWander.description: Optional +/- noise amplitude of the foot line in metres.

footZ.description: z of the skyline foot at x = 0: the line in front of which districts sit and behind which the skyline elements stand.

fogStartZ.description: z where the fog fade begins (elements behind it are paler).

fogOpaqueZ.description: z where the fog is fully opaque; nothing behind it is drawn.

rows.description: z positions of the element rows, front to back (e.g. [-78, -88, -96]). The front row appears at band 0; `growth[band].rows` says how many rows exist at each band. Use one entry for single-row skylines.

growth.description: Skyline state by band. `count` and `height` are what the generic renderer uses; family-specific breakdowns (halls, towers, gantries, chimneys...) sit beside them and must be consistent with `count`/`height`. Heights must be non-decreasing by band (validated).

0.description: State at 0 % course fraction: the minimum silhouette.

extras.description: Family-specific skyline parameters the generic renderer ignores (pitch, first x, footprints, materials, named towers).

coastCliff.description: How every land edge over water is cut: a vertical riser of `height` metres in `color` (the cross-section that also becomes the marker pedestal side), optionally with a horizontal band (coping course, piling band, light strip).

height.description: Vertical drop in metres from settled ground to the water (normally groundHeight - seaLevel).

material.description: Palette role name of the cliff face (a key of `palette`, validated).

band.description: One horizontal band on the riser: a coping course at the lip, a piling band at the waterline, or a light strip.

at.description: Where the band sits on the riser.

emissive.description: True if the band glows at night.

description.description: Notes on shore variants (terrace steps, slopes instead of cliffs, etc.).

extras.description: Family-specific land features the generic renderer ignores but the family renderer may read (slag shore terraces, open lawns that are not districts, river details).

water.description: Every water body. The open sea / lagoon uses geometry kind `complement` (everything outside land.outline and soloIsland); rivers and canals are polygons or polylines with a width; ponds and pools are discs.

id.description: Unique id of the water body within the file.

kind.description: Water kind: sea (open harbour water), lake, river (flowing, one direction), canal (built banks, boats), basin (small built pond or pool), lagoon (shallow clear sea).
Centreline swept by a width (rivers, canals).

innerRadius.description: Optional inner radius for a ring pool (dry disc in the middle).

kind.description: Everything outside land.outline and soloIsland: the open sea or lagoon.

nightColor.description: Night water colour, if it differs from the bible default.

deepColor.description: Deeper tint used far from shore (lagoons).

shallowsColor.description: Pale tint within a few metres of shore (lagoons).

material.description: Palette role name of the colour (a key of `palette`, validated).

flow.description: Flow direction for rivers/canals: east, west, north (toward -z), south (toward +z).

flowSpeed.description: Surface flow speed in m/s for the shader.

description.description: Notes on the body (what it is, far bank, how it joins other water).

extras.description: Family-specific water details (turning basin, lift bridge, etc.).

soloIsland.description: The second, solitary island (fix plan: 'the research station is the exception: alone on its own, bigger, island'). Null if the biome has none. Its district is listed in `districts` with `solitary: true` and referenced by `district`. Must be >= 15 m from every non-solitary district (validated).

district.description: Id of the district that sits on the island (that district has `solitary: true`).

radius.description: Nominal radius in metres (biome-layout.ts `miniIsland.radius`); the polygon, if given, is the real outline.

polygon.description: Island outline [x, z] at settled-ground height.

feature.description: What stands on the island and how it reads at 48 px (the anchor that exists at 0 %).

population.description: Buildings on the island by band; normally identical to its district's population.

material.description: Palette role of the island's cliff / wall (a key of `palette`, validated).

offshoreGap.description: Clear water in metres between the island and the nearest mainland shore (fix plan: 25-35 m).

access.description: How residents reach it: boat route, causeway, transit; never a bridge that reads as a road.

transit.description: Linear infrastructure: monorails, rails, roads, paths, causeways, pipe racks, conveyors. Each is a polyline with a width and an elevation above settled ground. Optional; local paths inside districts need not be listed.

id.description: Unique id of the line within the file.

kind.description: monorail (elevated pods), rail (freight/passenger rails at grade), road (vehicles), path (pedestrian paving), causeway (a low crossing over water), pipe (elevated pipe rack), conveyor (moving belt).

closed.description: True if the route is a loop (last point joins the first).

width.description: Width in metres (rail gauge for rails, beam width for monorails, pipe diameter for pipes). Null if the designer has not specified it yet (listed under Gaps).

edgeWidth.description: Optional total width including kerbs / edge bands, metres.

elevation.description: Height of the running surface above settled ground, metres (0 for roads and paths).

material.description: Palette role of the surface (a key of `palette`, validated).

appearsAtBand.description: Course-fraction band at which this line first exists (omit for always-present).

at.description: Stop position [x, z]; should be a vertex of `polyline`.

description.description: What runs on it and why it is there.

extras.description: Family-specific details (pods, pylon spacing, belt speed, water crossings, lamp spacing).

districts.description: Four to six large, multi-purpose districts shaped by the land (polygons or strips, never circles), each recognisable by its anchor with buildings hidden. Every pair must be >= 20 m apart (strips expanded by width / 2). Sorted by `band`.

name.description: Display name for the region panel.

band.description: Topic slot: course order from the arrival district (1) outward. Several topics map onto one district when a course has more topics than districts.

solitary.description: True for the district on `soloIsland`; it is exempt from the soloIsland distance rule.

shape.description: District region (biome-layout.ts `DistrictShape`): a polygon with >= 5 distinct vertices, or a strip (centreline + width). Circles are forbidden (validated).

vertices.description: Vertices [x, z], any winding, >= 5 distinct points (collinear points are allowed to keep a rectangle's shape).

kind.description: Strip region: the centreline offset both ways by width / 2 (biome-layout.ts `stripPolygon`).

fittedTo.description: The land feature the shape follows (a shore, a river bank, the skyline foot, a rail spine).

material.description: Palette role of the district's ground / dominant building material (biome-layout.ts `material`). Must be a key of `palette` (validated).

anchor.description: The one thing present at 0 % that identifies the district at 48 px with every building hidden (fix plan §2).

id.description: Slug naming the anchor object (e.g. quay-crane, boathouse-dock).

description.description: What the anchor is, with dimensions (biome-layout.ts `anchor` blurb).

position.description: Anchor position [x, z], or null if not yet placed by the designer.

footprint.description: Ground footprint [width, depth] in metres of the anchor group, or null if unknown (listed under Gaps).

silhouette48.description: How the anchor reads at 48 px with buildings hidden, in words.

features.description: Everything the district contains at 100 %, one string per feature, with counts and metres.

building.description: Kind of the counted building (biome-layout.ts `BuildingKind`), kebab-case.

buildingHeight.description: [min, max] height in metres of the counted building kind.

population.description: Building count by band (biome-layout.ts `PopulationTable`): 0 % anchor only; 25 % first buildings and the warm accent; 50 % half plus fences and lamps; 75 % all buildings plus clutter and string lights; 100 % extras. Non-decreasing (validated).

populationNotes.description: What each band adds, in words (props, lights, ambient), for the panel and for the family renderer.

props.description: Named prop counts by band that scale alongside the buildings (stalls, containers, trees, valves...).

extras100.description: The 100 % extras beyond the building count (second dock, watchtower, vehicles, string lights): one string each.

accent.description: The one warm accent per district, shown from 25 % ('first light').

object.description: Which object carries the accent colour.

camera.description: District station framing that satisfies the scale rule.

pitchDeg.description: Camera pitch above the ground plane, degrees.

azimuthDeg.description: Camera azimuth, degrees from +z toward +x (same convention as stationAzimuth).

fitWidth.description: Fraction of the frame width the district's chord fills.

laneYaw.description: Lane direction in radians from +z toward +x, used to lay building rows in polygon districts (biome-layout.ts `laneYaw`).

stationAzimuth.description: District-station azimuth in degrees from +z toward +x; long districts are framed along their length (biome-layout.ts `stationAzimuth`).

extras.description: Family-specific district data the generic renderer ignores.

landmark.description: The grand landmark on its own plinth (headland, slab, court) that evolves s1 -> s2 -> s3 with the course fraction (bible §a). Plinth must be >= 15 m from every district (validated).

name.description: Display name of the finished landmark.

plinth.description: The fixed base the landmark stands on: a disc (`radius`) or an explicit `polygon`, `height` above settled ground. Never changes with progress.

kind.description: Plinth form in words (12-facet court, slab with causeway, headland).

polygon.description: Plinth outline [x, z] when it is not round.

facets.description: Number of facets for a faceted round plinth.

height.description: Plinth top above settled ground, metres.

material.description: Palette role of the plinth (a key of `palette`, validated).

causeway.description: Outline of a causeway joining the plinth to the mainland, if any.

steps.description: Steps and links onto the plinth, in words.

stages.description: The three built stages. Stage from course fraction: 0 -> stake, < 0.5 -> s1, < 1 -> s2, 1 -> s3 (biome-layout.ts `landmarkStage`).

ruin.description: Catastrophe ruin state of the landmark and its recovery.

id.description: Catalog id of the ruin asset.

ipNote.description: How the design differs from the real-world reference it echoes.

marker.description: The globe marker: the biome's 48 px summary per globe-markers.md §3. A stacked pedestal in the ground material with 2-4 signature props in fixed slots; no signpost, no text.

side.description: Pedestal side colour (= the coast cliff / cross-section colour).

top.description: Pedestal top colour (= the dominant ground colour).

rim.description: Rim treatment in words (coping course, riveted band, glass strip).

props.description: Signature props in fixed slot order P1 (8 m) .. P4 (4 m).

slot.description: Slot name; P1 is the tallest and reads first.

height.description: Prop height in metres on the marker (8 / 6 / 4.8 / 4 by slot).

colours.description: All flat colours on the prop, primary first (2-3 plus accent).

accent.description: Accent colour on this prop, or null.

direction.description: Unit-ish direction [x, z] from the pedestal centre where the prop stands.

description.description: What the prop is, in words.

accent.description: The single accent object on the marker.

object.description: Which prop part carries the accent.

signpost.description: Always false: the course code lives in the HTML card.

silhouette48.description: What the marker reads as at 48 px, in words.

night.description: Night emissives on the marker (the pedestal never emits).

ambient.description: Always-on ambient layers (residents, boats, smoke, creature events, night order). Free-form; read by the family renderer only.

catastrophe.description: Family skin of the fixed catastrophe sequence: weather rolls in, residents fall apart, a family-specific ruin state, recovery.

creatureRoster.description: Creature accent colours that contrast with the ground, and colours to avoid.

avoid.description: Colours to avoid, with the reason.

point.description: [x, z] in metres; x east, z south.

polygon.description: Closed outline as ordered [x, z] points (>= 3), no repeated closing point.

count.description: Number of primary skyline elements in the front row (peaks, gantries, spires, halls).

height.description: Tallest skyline element at this band, metres. Non-decreasing by band.

rows.description: How many of `skyline.rows` exist at this band.

additionalProperties.description: Family-specific breakdown (halls, hallHeight, towers, chimneys, coolingTowers, bandsLit, moving...).

height.description: Total height in metres at this stage.

persists.description: Parts kept from the previous stage (empty for s1 means only the plinth).

grows.description: Parts that grow or are added at this stage.

lights.description: Parts that light up at night at this stage.

extras.description: Free-form object for family-specific design intent the generic renderer ignores. Keep it small and describe each key in a sibling `description` or `note` where possible.
